about: Hand-written query pairs over nested data (ARRAY, STRUCT, UNNEST) in GA4, Snowplow and shop schemas; see README.md.

events.event_params: ARRAY<STRUCT<key STRING, value STRUCT<string_value STRING, int_value INT64>>>
events.items: ARRAY<STRUCT<item_id STRING, quantity INT64, price FLOAT64>>

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name, (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'page_location') AS page FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT e.event_name, (SELECT p.value.string_value FROM UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p WHERE p.key = 'page_location') AS page FROM events AS e
pairs.note: The same lookup with the UNNEST element named and every column qualified.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name, (SELECT value.int_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'ga_session_id') AS session_id FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_name, (SELECT value.int_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE 'ga_session_id' = key) AS session_id FROM events
pairs.note: The key test written the other way round.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_name, (SELECT value.int_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'ga_session_id') AS v FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_name, (SELECT value.int_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'ga_session_number') AS v FROM events
pairs.note: Trap: a different parameter.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_name, (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'page_location') AS v FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_name, (SELECT CAST(value.int_value AS STRING) FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'page_location') AS v FROM events
pairs.note: Trap: the integer field instead of the string field of the same parameter.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name, (SELECT MAX(value.int_value) FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'engagement_time_msec') AS t FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_name, (SELECT MAX(IF(key = 'engagement_time_msec', value.int_value, NULL)) FROM UNNEST(event_params)) AS t FROM events
pairs.note: A filtered MAX against MAX of IF: MAX skips the NULLs that IF gives other keys, and both are NULL without a match.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_name, (SELECT MAX(value.int_value) FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'engagement_time_msec') AS t FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_name, (SELECT MIN(value.int_value) FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'engagement_time_msec') AS t FROM events
pairs.note: Trap: a key that repeats with two values.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_name, (SELECT SUM(value.int_value) FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'engagement_time_msec') AS t FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_name, (SELECT MAX(value.int_value) FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'engagement_time_msec') AS t FROM events
pairs.note: Trap: SUM and MAX part when a key repeats.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'page_location' AND value.string_value = 'home')
pairs.right: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE 'home' IN (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'page_location')
pairs.note: EXISTS and IN over the same parameter rows.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT e.user_pseudo_id FROM events AS e, UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p WHERE p.key = 'page_location' AND p.value.string_value = 'home'
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT user_pseudo_id FROM events WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(event_params) AS p WHERE p.key = 'page_location' AND p.value.string_value = 'home')
pairs.note: Under DISTINCT, joining the parameters and testing that one exists are the same.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT e.user_pseudo_id FROM events AS e, UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p WHERE p.key = 'page_location' AND p.value.string_value = 'home'
pairs.right: SELECT user_pseudo_id FROM events WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(event_params) AS p WHERE p.key = 'page_location' AND p.value.string_value = 'home')
pairs.note: Trap: without DISTINCT, an event with two matching parameters gives two rows on the left.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT e.event_name, p.key FROM events AS e CROSS JOIN UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p
pairs.right: SELECT e.event_name, p.key FROM events AS e LEFT JOIN UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p
pairs.note: Trap: LEFT JOIN keeps an event with no parameters.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT e.event_name, p.key FROM events AS e, UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p
pairs.right: SELECT e.event_name, p.key FROM events AS e CROSS JOIN UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p
pairs.note: Comma and CROSS JOIN are the same join.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT e.event_name, p.key FROM events AS e CROSS JOIN UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p
pairs.right: SELECT e.event_name, p.key FROM events AS e JOIN UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p ON TRUE
pairs.note: An inner join on TRUE is a cross join.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT e.event_name, p.key FROM events AS e LEFT JOIN UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p WHERE p.key IS NOT NULL
pairs.right: SELECT e.event_name, p.key FROM events AS e CROSS JOIN UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p WHERE p.key IS NOT NULL
pairs.note: A WHERE test that rejects NULL removes every padded row, so the LEFT JOIN is an inner one.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT e.event_name, p.key FROM events AS e LEFT JOIN UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p WHERE p.key IS NULL
pairs.right: SELECT e.event_name, p.key FROM events AS e CROSS JOIN UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p WHERE p.key IS NULL
pairs.note: Trap: IS NULL keeps the padded row of an event with no parameters.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT e.event_name, p.key FROM (SELECT * FROM events WHERE event_name = 'page_view') AS e, UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p
pairs.right: SELECT e.event_name, p.key FROM events AS e, UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p WHERE e.event_name = 'page_view'
pairs.note: A filter on the event moved into a derived table that is then unnested.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT e.event_name, p.value.int_value AS v FROM events AS e, UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p WHERE p.key = 'ga_session_id' AND e.event_name = 'page_view'
pairs.right: SELECT e.event_name, p.value.int_value AS v FROM events AS e, UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p WHERE e.event_name = 'page_view' AND p.key = 'ga_session_id'
pairs.note: The same conjuncts in another order.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT e.event_name, (SELECT MAX(value.int_value) FROM UNNEST(e.event_params) WHERE key = 'ga_session_id') AS v FROM events AS e
pairs.right: SELECT e.event_name, p.value.int_value AS v FROM events AS e LEFT JOIN UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p ON p.key = 'ga_session_id'
pairs.note: Trap: a repeated key gives one row on the left and two on the right.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT e.user_pseudo_id, MAX(IF(p.key = 'ga_session_id', p.value.int_value, NULL)) AS v FROM events AS e LEFT JOIN UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p GROUP BY e.user_pseudo_id
pairs.right: SELECT e.user_pseudo_id, (SELECT MAX(IF(key = 'ga_session_id', value.int_value, NULL)) FROM UNNEST(e.event_params)) AS v FROM events AS e
pairs.note: Trap: grouping by user merges that user's events; the lookup keeps one row per event.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name, ARRAY_LENGTH(event_params) AS n FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_name, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM UNNEST(event_params)) AS n FROM events
pairs.note: A stored array is never NULL (BigQuery stores NULL as an empty array), so its length is the number of rows UNNEST gives.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_name, ARRAY_LENGTH(event_params) AS n FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_name, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT key) FROM UNNEST(event_params)) AS n FROM events
pairs.note: Trap: a repeated key.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE ARRAY_LENGTH(event_params) > 0
pairs.right: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(event_params))
pairs.note: A non-empty array is one that UNNEST gives a row for.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE ARRAY_LENGTH(event_params) > 0
pairs.right: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE event_params IS NOT NULL
pairs.note: Trap: a stored array is never NULL, but it can be empty.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name, (SELECT SUM(i.quantity) FROM UNNEST(items) AS i) AS q FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_name, (SELECT SUM(quantity) FROM UNNEST(items)) AS q FROM events
pairs.note: A field read through the element's name or directly.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_name, (SELECT SUM(quantity) FROM UNNEST(items)) AS q FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_name, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM UNNEST(items)) AS q FROM events
pairs.note: Trap: quantities against item rows.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT device.category AS category FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT e.device.category AS category FROM events AS e
pairs.note: A struct field read with and without the table's name.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT device.category AS v FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT device.operating_system AS v FROM events
pairs.note: Trap: another field.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE geo = STRUCT('US' AS country, 'NYC' AS city)
pairs.right: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE geo.country = 'US' AND geo.city = 'NYC'
pairs.note: Struct equality compares field by field, NULL when a field is NULL and none differs: the same as AND of the field tests.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE geo.country = 'US'
pairs.right: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE geo = STRUCT('US' AS country, CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS city)
pairs.note: Trap: comparing with a NULL field is never TRUE.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE geo IS NULL
pairs.right: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE geo.country IS NULL AND geo.city IS NULL
pairs.note: Trap: a struct whose fields are all NULL is not NULL itself.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name, IF(geo IS NULL, NULL, geo.country) AS country FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_name, geo.country AS country FROM events
pairs.note: A field of a NULL struct is NULL.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE event_name IN UNNEST(['page_view', 'scroll'])
pairs.right: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE event_name IN ('page_view', 'scroll')
pairs.note: IN UNNEST of a literal array is an IN list.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE event_name NOT IN UNNEST(['page_view', 'scroll'])
pairs.right: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE event_name NOT IN ('page_view', 'scroll')
pairs.note: NOT IN UNNEST of a literal array is a NOT IN list (both NULL for a NULL name).

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(event_params) AS a WHERE a.key = 'session_engaged')
pairs.right: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(event_params) AS b WHERE b.key = 'session_engaged')
pairs.note: Only the element's name differs.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'session_engaged')
pairs.right: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'session_engaged') > 0
pairs.note: A positive count of matching parameters is EXISTS.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'session_engaged') > 0
pairs.right: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'session_engaged') > 1
pairs.note: Trap: one matching parameter.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'session_engaged') = 0
pairs.right: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'session_engaged')
pairs.note: A zero count is NOT EXISTS.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name, ARRAY(SELECT DISTINCT key FROM UNNEST(event_params) ORDER BY key) AS keys FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_name, ARRAY(SELECT key FROM UNNEST(event_params) GROUP BY key ORDER BY key) AS keys FROM events
pairs.note: DISTINCT and GROUP BY give the same sorted keys.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_name, ARRAY(SELECT DISTINCT key FROM UNNEST(event_params) ORDER BY key) AS keys FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_name, ARRAY(SELECT key FROM UNNEST(event_params) ORDER BY key) AS keys FROM events
pairs.note: Trap: a repeated key appears twice on the right.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM events AS e, UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p
pairs.right: SELECT IFNULL(SUM(ARRAY_LENGTH(event_params)), 0) AS n FROM events
pairs.note: Counting unnested rows is summing the array lengths (0 over no events).

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM events AS e, UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p
pairs.right: SELECT SUM(ARRAY_LENGTH(event_params)) AS n FROM events
pairs.note: Trap: over no events COUNT is 0 and SUM is NULL.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT p.key, COUNT(*) AS n FROM events AS e, UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p GROUP BY p.key
pairs.right: SELECT key, COUNT(*) AS n FROM events, UNNEST(event_params) GROUP BY key
pairs.note: The element named or not.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT p.key, COUNT(*) AS n FROM events AS e, UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p GROUP BY p.key
pairs.right: SELECT p.key, COUNT(DISTINCT e.user_pseudo_id) AS n FROM events AS e, UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p GROUP BY p.key
pairs.note: Trap: rows against distinct users.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_name FROM events WHERE 'home' IN (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'page_location')
pairs.right: SELECT event_name FROM events AS e WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(e.event_params) AS p WHERE p.key = 'page_location' AND p.value.string_value = 'home')
pairs.note: An IN subquery over the parameters is an EXISTS with the comparison added.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_id, contexts_web_page[SAFE_OFFSET(0)].id AS page_view_id FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_id, contexts_web_page[SAFE_ORDINAL(1)].id AS page_view_id FROM events
pairs.note: Offset 0 is ordinal 1.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_id, contexts_web_page[SAFE_OFFSET(1)].id AS page_view_id FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_id, contexts_web_page[SAFE_ORDINAL(1)].id AS page_view_id FROM events
pairs.note: Trap: offset 1 is the second element.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_id, contexts_web_page[SAFE_OFFSET(0)].id AS page_view_id FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_id, (SELECT c.id FROM UNNEST(contexts_web_page) AS c WITH OFFSET AS o WHERE o = 0) AS page_view_id FROM events
pairs.note: The first element read by subscript or by UNNEST WITH OFFSET.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_id, contexts_web_page[SAFE_OFFSET(0)].id AS page_view_id FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_id, (SELECT MIN(c.id) FROM UNNEST(contexts_web_page) AS c) AS page_view_id FROM events
pairs.note: Trap: the first element is not the smallest.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_id, (SELECT ua.useragent_family FROM UNNEST(contexts_ua) AS ua WITH OFFSET AS o WHERE o = 0) AS family FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_id, contexts_ua[SAFE_OFFSET(0)].useragent_family AS family FROM events
pairs.note: The first user-agent context, two ways.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_id FROM events WHERE ARRAY_LENGTH(contexts_web_page) > 0
pairs.right: SELECT event_id FROM events WHERE contexts_web_page[SAFE_OFFSET(0)] IS NOT NULL
pairs.note: A stored array holds no NULL element, so a first element exists exactly when the array is not empty.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_id FROM events WHERE ARRAY_LENGTH(contexts_web_page) > 0
pairs.right: SELECT event_id FROM events WHERE contexts_web_page[SAFE_OFFSET(0)].id IS NOT NULL
pairs.note: Trap: the first element can have a NULL id.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_id, ARRAY_LENGTH(contexts_web_page) AS n FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT event_id, ARRAY_LENGTH(contexts_ua) AS n FROM events
pairs.note: Trap: another context.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT s.domain_userid, c.id FROM events AS s, UNNEST(s.contexts_web_page) AS c
pairs.right: SELECT s.domain_userid, c.id FROM events AS s, UNNEST(s.contexts_web_page) AS c GROUP BY 1, 2
pairs.note: DISTINCT is GROUP BY on every output.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_id FROM events WHERE 'Chrome' IN (SELECT useragent_family FROM UNNEST(contexts_ua))
pairs.right: SELECT event_id FROM events AS s WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(s.contexts_ua) AS u WHERE u.useragent_family = 'Chrome')
pairs.note: IN over a field of the elements is EXISTS.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT event_id FROM events WHERE unstruct_link_click IS NOT NULL AND unstruct_link_click.target_url = 'https://example.com'
pairs.right: SELECT event_id FROM events WHERE unstruct_link_click.target_url = 'https://example.com'
pairs.note: A field of a NULL struct is NULL, so the IS NOT NULL test adds nothing.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT event_id FROM events WHERE unstruct_link_click IS NOT NULL
pairs.right: SELECT event_id FROM events WHERE unstruct_link_click.target_url IS NOT NULL
pairs.note: Trap: a click struct with a NULL URL.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT unstruct_link_click.element_id AS element FROM events
pairs.right: SELECT s.unstruct_link_click.element_id AS element FROM events AS s
pairs.note: A struct field with and without the table's name.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT s.event_id, u.os_family FROM events AS s, UNNEST(s.contexts_ua) AS u WHERE u.useragent_family = 'Chrome'
pairs.right: SELECT s.event_id, u.os_family FROM events AS s JOIN UNNEST(s.contexts_ua) AS u ON u.useragent_family = 'Chrome'
pairs.note: A filter on the element in WHERE or in the join's ON.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT s.event_id, u.os_family FROM events AS s, UNNEST(s.contexts_ua) AS u WHERE u.useragent_family = 'Chrome'
pairs.right: SELECT s.event_id, u.os_family FROM events AS s LEFT JOIN UNNEST(s.contexts_ua) AS u ON u.useragent_family = 'Chrome'
pairs.note: Trap: a LEFT JOIN's ON keeps events without a Chrome context.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT order_id FROM orders WHERE 'gift' IN UNNEST(tags)
pairs.right: SELECT order_id FROM orders AS o WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(o.tags) AS t WHERE t = 'gift')
pairs.note: IN UNNEST is an existence test.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT order_id FROM orders WHERE NOT 'gift' IN UNNEST(tags)
pairs.right: SELECT order_id FROM orders AS o WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(o.tags) AS t WHERE t = 'gift')
pairs.note: A stored array holds no NULL element and the constant is not NULL, so IN UNNEST is never NULL here.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT order_id FROM orders AS o WHERE NOT CAST(o.customer_id AS STRING) IN UNNEST(o.tags)
pairs.right: SELECT order_id FROM orders AS o WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(o.tags) AS t WHERE t = CAST(o.customer_id AS STRING))
pairs.note: Trap: a NULL left side makes IN UNNEST NULL for a non-empty array, so NOT IN drops the row that NOT EXISTS keeps.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT order_id FROM orders AS o WHERE CAST(o.customer_id AS STRING) IN UNNEST(o.tags)
pairs.right: SELECT order_id FROM orders AS o WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(o.tags) AS t WHERE t = CAST(o.customer_id AS STRING))
pairs.note: In WHERE, NULL and FALSE both drop the row.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id, 90 IN UNNEST(scores) AS top FROM customers
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(scores) AS s WHERE s = 90) AS top FROM customers
pairs.note: As a value too: the constant is not NULL and a stored array holds no NULL element.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id, customer_id IN UNNEST(scores) AS hit FROM customers
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(scores) AS s WHERE s = customer_id) AS hit FROM customers
pairs.note: Trap: for a NULL customer_id and a non-empty array the left is NULL and the right FALSE.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT o.order_id, l.sku FROM orders AS o, UNNEST(o.lines) AS l WHERE l.qty > 1
pairs.right: SELECT o.order_id, l.sku FROM orders AS o CROSS JOIN UNNEST(o.lines) AS l WHERE l.qty > 1
pairs.note: Comma and CROSS JOIN.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT o.order_id, SUM(l.qty) AS units FROM orders AS o LEFT JOIN UNNEST(o.lines) AS l GROUP BY o.order_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, (SELECT SUM(qty) FROM UNNEST(lines)) AS units FROM orders
pairs.note: With order_id a key, grouping the unnested lines by order is a per-order subquery (NULL for no lines on both sides).

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT o.order_id, SUM(l.qty) AS units FROM orders AS o LEFT JOIN UNNEST(o.lines) AS l GROUP BY o.order_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, (SELECT SUM(qty) FROM UNNEST(lines)) AS units FROM orders
pairs.note: Trap: without a key, two orders with one id merge on the left.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT o.order_id, COUNT(l.sku) AS n FROM orders AS o LEFT JOIN UNNEST(o.lines) AS l GROUP BY o.order_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, (SELECT COUNT(sku) FROM UNNEST(lines)) AS n FROM orders
pairs.note: COUNT of a field is 0 for an order without lines on both sides.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT o.order_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders AS o LEFT JOIN UNNEST(o.lines) AS l GROUP BY o.order_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM UNNEST(lines)) AS n FROM orders
pairs.note: Trap: COUNT(*) counts the padded row of an order without lines.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT o.order_id, ARRAY_AGG(t ORDER BY off) AS tags FROM orders AS o, UNNEST(o.tags) AS t WITH OFFSET AS off GROUP BY o.order_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, tags FROM orders WHERE ARRAY_LENGTH(tags) > 0
pairs.note: Unnesting and re-aggregating in offset order rebuilds each non-empty array (order_id is a key).

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT o.order_id, ARRAY_AGG(t ORDER BY off) AS tags FROM orders AS o, UNNEST(o.tags) AS t WITH OFFSET AS off GROUP BY o.order_id
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, tags FROM orders
pairs.note: Trap: an order without tags has no row on the left.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT order_id, ARRAY(SELECT t FROM UNNEST(tags) AS t WITH OFFSET AS off ORDER BY off) AS tags FROM orders
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, tags FROM orders
pairs.note: Rebuilding an array in offset order gives the array.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT order_id, ARRAY(SELECT t FROM UNNEST(tags) AS t) AS tags FROM orders
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, tags FROM orders
pairs.note: Trap: without ORDER BY the element order is BigQuery's to pick.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT order_id, ARRAY(SELECT DISTINCT t FROM UNNEST(tags) AS t ORDER BY t) AS tags FROM orders
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, ARRAY(SELECT t FROM UNNEST(tags) AS t ORDER BY t) AS tags FROM orders
pairs.note: Trap: a repeated tag.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT order_id, ARRAY_LENGTH(ARRAY(SELECT t FROM UNNEST(tags) AS t WHERE t <> 'gift')) AS n FROM orders
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM UNNEST(tags) AS t WHERE t <> 'gift') AS n FROM orders
pairs.note: The length of a filtered array is the count of the filtered elements.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT order_id, ARRAY_LENGTH(ARRAY_CONCAT(tags, ['x'])) AS n FROM orders
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, ARRAY_LENGTH(tags) + 1 AS n FROM orders
pairs.note: Concatenation adds lengths (a stored array is never NULL).

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT order_id, ARRAY_CONCAT(tags, ['x']) AS t FROM orders
pairs.right: SELECT order_id, ARRAY_CONCAT(['x'], tags) AS t FROM orders
pairs.note: Trap: element order.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT ship.city AS city FROM orders
pairs.right: SELECT orders.ship.city AS city FROM orders
pairs.note: A struct field with and without the table's name.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT STRUCT(o.order_id AS id, o.customer_id AS c).c AS c FROM orders AS o
pairs.right: SELECT o.customer_id AS c FROM orders AS o
pairs.note: A field of a struct built in place is the expression it was built from.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT STRUCT(o.order_id AS id, o.customer_id AS c).id AS c FROM orders AS o
pairs.right: SELECT o.customer_id AS c FROM orders AS o
pairs.note: Trap: the other field.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT (SELECT AS STRUCT o.order_id AS id, o.customer_id AS c).id AS id FROM orders AS o
pairs.right: SELECT o.order_id AS id FROM orders AS o
pairs.note: A field of a SELECT AS STRUCT row.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT d.s.city AS city FROM (SELECT STRUCT(ship.city AS city, order_id AS id) AS s FROM orders) AS d
pairs.right: SELECT ship.city AS city FROM orders
pairs.note: A field of a struct built in a derived table.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT o.order_id, c.name FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id, UNNEST(o.tags) AS t WHERE t = 'gift'
pairs.right: SELECT o.order_id, c.name FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE 'gift' IN UNNEST(o.tags)
pairs.note: Trap: an order tagged gift twice gives two rows on the left.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT o.order_id, c.name FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id, UNNEST(o.tags) AS t WHERE t = 'gift'
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT o.order_id, c.name FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE 'gift' IN UNNEST(o.tags)
pairs.note: Under DISTINCT the repeated rows do not show.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT o.order_id, l.sku, c.name FROM orders AS o, UNNEST(o.lines) AS l JOIN customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
pairs.right: SELECT o.order_id, l.sku, c.name FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id, UNNEST(o.lines) AS l
pairs.note: The UNNEST and the join in either order.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT c.customer_id, MAX(s) AS best FROM customers AS c, UNNEST(c.scores) AS s GROUP BY c.customer_id
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, (SELECT MAX(s) FROM UNNEST(scores) AS s) AS best FROM customers WHERE ARRAY_LENGTH(scores) > 0
pairs.note: Grouping unnested scores by a key is a per-customer subquery over customers with scores.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT c.customer_id, MAX(s) AS best FROM customers AS c, UNNEST(c.scores) AS s GROUP BY c.customer_id
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, (SELECT MAX(s) FROM UNNEST(scores) AS s) AS best FROM customers
pairs.note: Trap: a customer without scores has a row only on the right.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id, scores[SAFE_OFFSET(ARRAY_LENGTH(scores) - 1)] AS last FROM customers
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, ARRAY_REVERSE(scores)[SAFE_OFFSET(0)] AS last FROM customers
pairs.note: The last element two ways.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id, scores[SAFE_OFFSET(0)] AS last FROM customers
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, ARRAY_REVERSE(scores)[SAFE_OFFSET(0)] AS last FROM customers
pairs.note: Trap: first against last.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id, (SELECT MAX(s) FROM UNNEST(scores) AS s) AS best FROM customers
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, (SELECT s FROM UNNEST(scores) AS s ORDER BY s DESC LIMIT 1) AS best FROM customers
pairs.note: The top element of a sorted array is its MAX (stored arrays hold no NULL; ties give the same value).

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id, (SELECT MIN(s) FROM UNNEST(scores) AS s) AS best FROM customers
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, (SELECT s FROM UNNEST(scores) AS s ORDER BY s DESC LIMIT 1) AS best FROM customers
pairs.note: Trap: MIN against the top element.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(scores) AS s WHERE s > 90)
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE (SELECT MAX(s) FROM UNNEST(scores) AS s) > 90
pairs.note: In WHERE, some score above 90 is a MAX above 90 (NULL for no scores drops the row like FALSE).

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id, EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(scores) AS s WHERE s > 90) AS high FROM customers
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, (SELECT MAX(s) FROM UNNEST(scores) AS s) > 90 AS high FROM customers
pairs.note: Trap: as a value, no scores is FALSE on the left and NULL on the right.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT c.customer_id, e FROM customers AS c, UNNEST(c.emails) AS e WHERE e = 'a@example.com'
pairs.right: SELECT c.customer_id, e FROM customers AS c CROSS JOIN UNNEST(c.emails) AS e WHERE 'a@example.com' = e
pairs.note: The same filter on the element.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT c.customer_id, s FROM customers AS c, UNNEST(c.scores) AS s WITH OFFSET AS i WHERE i < 2
pairs.right: SELECT c.customer_id, s FROM customers AS c, UNNEST(c.scores) AS s WITH OFFSET AS i WHERE i <= 1
pairs.note: Offsets are whole numbers.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT c.customer_id, s FROM customers AS c, UNNEST(c.scores) AS s WITH OFFSET AS i WHERE i < 2
pairs.right: SELECT c.customer_id, s FROM customers AS c, UNNEST(c.scores) AS s WITH OFFSET AS i WHERE i < 1
pairs.note: Trap: the second element.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id FROM customers AS c, UNNEST(c.scores) AS s WHERE s > 50
pairs.right: SELECT c.customer_id FROM customers AS c, UNNEST(c.scores) AS s WHERE s > 50
pairs.note: Trap: two scores above 50 give two rows.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT x FROM UNNEST([1, 2, 3]) AS x
pairs.right: SELECT 1 AS x UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3
pairs.note: UNNEST of a literal array is its elements.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT x FROM UNNEST([1, 2, 2]) AS x
pairs.right: SELECT 1 AS x UNION DISTINCT SELECT 2
pairs.note: Trap: UNNEST keeps the repeated element.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE customer_id IN UNNEST([1, 2])
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE customer_id IN (1, 2)
pairs.note: IN UNNEST of a literal array is an IN list.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE customer_id NOT IN UNNEST([1, 2])
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE customer_id NOT IN (1, 2)
pairs.note: NOT IN UNNEST of a literal array is a NOT IN list.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE customer_id IN UNNEST([1, 2])
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE customer_id IN (1, 3)
pairs.note: Trap: another list.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT ARRAY_LENGTH([1, 2, 3]) AS n
pairs.right: SELECT 3 AS n
pairs.note: The length of a literal array.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT [10, 20, 30][OFFSET(1)] AS v
pairs.right: SELECT 20 AS v
pairs.note: An element of a literal array.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT [10, 20, 30][OFFSET(1)] AS v
pairs.right: SELECT [10, 20, 30][ORDINAL(1)] AS v
pairs.note: Trap: offset 1 against ordinal 1.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT x, o FROM UNNEST(['a', 'b']) AS x WITH OFFSET AS o
pairs.right: SELECT 'a' AS x, 0 AS o UNION ALL SELECT 'b', 1
pairs.note: WITH OFFSET counts from 0.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT x, o FROM UNNEST(['a', 'b']) AS x WITH OFFSET AS o
pairs.right: SELECT 'a' AS x, 1 AS o UNION ALL SELECT 'b', 2
pairs.note: Trap: offsets do not count from 1.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM UNNEST(CAST(NULL AS ARRAY<INT64>))) AS n
pairs.right: SELECT 0 AS n
pairs.note: UNNEST of a NULL array gives no rows.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT ARRAY_LENGTH(CAST(NULL AS ARRAY<INT64>)) AS n
pairs.right: SELECT 0 AS n
pairs.note: Trap: the length of a NULL array is NULL.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.left: SELECT STRUCT(1 AS a, 'x' AS b).b AS v
pairs.right: SELECT 'x' AS v
pairs.note: A field of a literal struct.

pairs.label: different
pairs.left: SELECT ARRAY_LENGTH(ARRAY_CONCAT(CAST(NULL AS ARRAY<INT64>), [1])) AS n
pairs.right: SELECT 1 AS n
pairs.note: Trap: ARRAY_CONCAT with a NULL array is NULL.
